t: The King and Head of the Church
s: Christ rules his church from his throne through Word and Spirit by the ministry of men, and has given it officers, oracles and ordinances, with nothing to be added or taken away.

Eight principles on liberty of conscience, a church’s right to set its own terms, discipline, the tie between truth and holiness, forbearance, election of officers, ministerial power and spiritual discipline.
The Constitution is the Westminster Confession and Catechisms together with the Book of Church Order, all subordinate to Scripture.
Five heads of the scriptural, representative form: the church, its members, its officers, its courts, its orders.
One visible church in every age; denominations that keep Word and sacraments in fundamental integrity are true branches.

t: The Nature and Extent of Church Power
s: Power vests in the whole body, is exercised severally as order and jointly as jurisdiction, is wholly spiritual, and is bounded by the law of Christ.
What a congregation is, who its officers are, where its jurisdiction sits, and what ordinances Christ has given it.

t: The Organization of a Particular Church
s: Mission churches, the temporary government a presbytery gives them, and the steps by which they are organized as particular churches.
Children of believers are non-communing members; those who profess faith, are baptized and are admitted by the Session are communing members.
Extraordinary offices ceased with the close of revelation; the perpetual classes are elders, in two orders, and deacons, open to men only.
Titles, qualifications and duties of the office, the added functions of teaching elders, evangelists, calls outside the church, chaplains, and the standing of ruling elders.
An office of sympathy and service under the Session, with care of the poor and of church property, and assistants who are not officers.
The courts are Sessions, presbyteries and the General Assembly; all are presbyteries in nature, with moderators, clerks and prayer.
Church courts are distinct from the magistrate, their power is ministerial and declarative, and lower courts are under the review and control of higher ones.
Who sits on a Session, what makes a quorum, who moderates, and the powers by which it governs a congregation.
Its make-up and representation, the membership of ministers, quorum, reception and transfer of ministers, and its powers over churches and officers.
The highest court: its organizing principles, permanent committees, make-up, quorum, powers, and the weight its actions carry.
A commission concludes business, unlike a committee; presbytery commissions, the Standing Judicial Commission and provisional presbyteries abroad.

t: Church Orders, The Doctrine of Vocation
s: Calling to office is inward testimony, the approval of God’s people and the judgment of a court, and no man is placed over a church without its election or consent.
Officers are inducted by the ordination of a court, with prayer and laying on of hands, and only to a definite work.
Coming under the care of a presbytery: the Session’s endorsement, examination on experiential religion, annual reports, dismissal and removal.
Licensure to preach, the questions put to a licentiate, the four-year term, and an internship of at least a year with its limits.
A call to definite work, the pulpit committee, the congregational election, the form of the call and its prosecution before presbytery.

t: The Ordination and Installation of Ministers
s: Education, the trials for ordination, examination of character, stated differences with the Standards, the vows, and the service itself.
Pastor, associate pastor and assistant pastor, and the temporary relations of stated, student and ruling elder supply.

t: Dissolution of the Pastoral Relation and Honorable Retirement
s: How a pastoral relation is dissolved by either party, the limit on an associate or assistant succeeding the pastor, retirement and pastor emeritus.

t: Election, Ordination and Installation of Ruling Elders and Deacons
s: Nomination, instruction and examination by the Session, the congregational election, the ordination service, and release from active duty.
Who votes, how meetings are called and by what quorum, trustees and corporations, and the property and withdrawal provisions.

t: Amending the Constitution of the Church
s: Three steps for the Book of Church Order, three-fourths at every step for the Confession and Catechisms, and the terms of organic union.

t: Discipline, Its Nature, Subjects and Ends
s: Discipline in two senses, its ends, the spirit in which it is used, and the scriptural steps that must be kept in order.
The nurture of covenant children by parents and church, and the care owed to adult non-communing members.
An offense is anything in doctrine or practice contrary to the Word; offenses are personal or general, private or public.
Admonition, suspension from the sacraments, excommunication, suspension from office and deposition, and when each is used.

t: The Parties in Cases of Process
s: Original jurisdiction, investigation of reports, the Church as accuser, the Matthew 18 requirement, cautions about accusers, and suspension of a court member under process.

t: General Provisions Applicable to all Cases of Process
s: Charges in writing, citations and their intervals, contumacy, the order of a trial, the Record of the Case, representation, and objection for lapse of time.

t: Special Rules Pertaining to Process Before Sessions
s: Members are tried by their own Session, with a route to presbytery in doctrinal cases and public scandal, and rules for contumacy and the Table.

t: Special Rules Pertaining to Process Against a Minister
s: A minister is tried by his presbytery, with a route to the Assembly, care about accusations, confession during trial, restoration, and divestiture without censure.
Competent witnesses, the accused not compelled to testify, accommodations by videoconference, the rule of more than one witness, oaths, and the recording of trials.
The manner of each censure, from private admonition to excommunication and deposition, and the raising of an indefinite suspension.
How censures are lifted and offenders restored, with special caution for ministers, and where jurisdiction sits.
Judgment on a written confession, divestiture at a minister’s own request, attempted withdrawal, and erasure for willful neglect.

t: Modes in Which Lower Courts Come Under the Supervision of Higher Courts
s: The four modes, the right of lower court members to sit above, and the four standards that govern review of judicial proceedings.
Annual review of records, the four questions reviewers ask, neglected duty, and citation of a lower court on a credible report.
A lower court may ask a higher one for advice or for disposition of a matter, including original jurisdiction or added elders.
Who may appeal, the grounds, the thirty-day notice, the effect on the judgment, the hearing, and the decisions open to the higher court.
Any communing member may complain of an act of a court over him; the filing periods, the effect, the hearing and the powers of the higher court.
This chapter was vacated and stands empty in the current book.
Three ways a member of a court puts his disagreement on the record, and the thirty-day window for filing.
Transfer of members between churches, associate members, dismissal of ministers, the life of a certificate, and assignment after divestiture.

part: Directory for the Worship of God
t: The Principles and Elements of Public Worship
s: Worship is shaped by Scripture alone; it is a meeting of God with his people; no fixed forms are prescribed, and the elements are listed.

part: Directory for the Worship of God
t: The Sanctification of the Lord’s Day
s: The whole day is kept holy in public and private exercises of religion, prepared for beforehand.

part: Directory for the Worship of God
s: The congregation gathers on time, in reverence, and families are encouraged to worship together.

part: Directory for the Worship of God
t: The Public Reading of the Holy Scriptures
s: Reading by the minister is God addressing his people; it is read from a good translation, not a paraphrase.

part: Directory for the Worship of God
t: The Singing of Psalms and Hymns
s: Praise in song is a duty and privilege; psalms are recommended alongside hymns, and a choir is not to displace the congregation.

part: Directory for the Worship of God
s: The parts of a full prayer before the sermon, the minister’s duty to prepare, and prayer in the language of the people.

part: Directory for the Worship of God
s: The text carries the doctrine, sermons are prepared with care and plainness, and no one preaches without the Session’s consent.

part: Directory for the Worship of God
t: The Worship of God by Offerings
s: God owns all and we are stewards; giving at least a tithe is part of acknowledging it, in regular and proportionate offerings.

part: Directory for the Worship of God
s: It is proper for the congregation to confess the faith publicly with creeds true to the Word.

part: Directory for the Worship of God
s: Baptism by a minister in the presence of the congregation under the Session, with instruction, parental vows and the mode of pouring or sprinkling. Carries full constitutional authority.

part: Directory for the Worship of God
t: The Admission of Persons to Sealing Ordinances
s: The Session judges readiness, unbaptized applicants profess and are baptized, and those admitted take five membership vows. Carries full constitutional authority.

part: Directory for the Worship of God
t: The Administration of the Lord’s Supper
s: Frequency is set by the Session, the ignorant and scandalous are not admitted, and the invitation follows one of two patterns. Carries full constitutional authority.

part: Directory for the Worship of God
s: Marriage is a divine institution though not a sacrament, and is only between one man and one woman. Section 59-3 carries full constitutional authority.

part: Directory for the Worship of God
s: Prayer for the sick, notice to the minister or an officer, and the pastor’s duty and discretion in visiting.

part: Directory for the Worship of God
s: Psalms or hymns, Scripture with remarks, and prayer for the bereaved, with the service left largely to the minister.

part: Directory for the Worship of God
s: Who may appoint such days, from families up to the General Assembly, and how they are to be kept.

part: Directory for the Worship of God
s: Secret worship and family worship as duties, with parents teaching and setting an example.
